Trading in the $160s, Nvidia's valuation has taken a big haircut, yet its underlying business fundamentals remain largely intact.

Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation has sent shockwaves through the tech sector, dragging Nvidia's (NVDA) stock down roughly 30% since Oct.
While Huang was the architect of Nvidia's AI dominance, the company's moat — superior GPUs, the CUDA software ecosystem, and networking expertise — does not walk out the door with him.
That's one thing at less than 10x forward earnings, as Nvidia is, or even at a market multiple.

Of the top 20 options trades by dollar-amount, 12 were Nvidia, the data show.
The net position, a bullish call spread, needs Nvidia to trade above around $206 by expiry, or about 15% higher, to be profitable.

AAPL: Jim Cramer is often found of saying that you own Apple , you don't trade it.
Apple's resilience continues to catch the attention of options traders looking for a safe harbor in tech.
Almost 900,000 options traded on Apple in the first half of the session Wednesday – almost 500,000 calls and 370,000 puts.
But Apple is twice as expensive as the S&P.
Apple has been priced at a steep premium for being immune to what ails other struggling stocks, but is now demonstrating similar vulnerabilities.
If the market suddenly decided that Apple's premium to the market would be just 50%, instead of 100%, that would be less than 28x forward earnings, a nearly 27% haircut to the current share price.
Apple implied volatility is actually just below the 1-year average.
Apple's historic premium is built on a foundation of immunity to the chaos infecting the rest of the market.

With Apple supported by an extraordinary string of recent product releases and massive free cash flow, but possibly suppressed by high valuations, this could be an excellent opportunity for a call spread risk reversal.
Ideally, you want Apple shares to stay between the two, short strikes by December expiration and above $360 by February expiration.

The two stocks have been on trajectories that are distinct from the broader AI trade – with Apple, in particular, trading almost inversely to the Nasdaq 100 Index – but that's not stopping speculators from betting on a reversal in their shares after earnings.

Right now, the implied move for Apple by the end of the week is less than $16.50, or under 4.8% of the current stock price, considerably higher than the 3.25% median move over the last four quarters.

Whether you are looking to hedge a long underlying equity position or simply want to speculate that Apple could become the latest casualty of a demanding earnings season, defining your risk is paramount.
